title: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White the press secretary job
caption: President Trump said on Truth Social on Nov. 7 that he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the job of White House press secretary. At a news conference in London, White said he was flying to Washington for a Monday meeting but did not say whether he would accept. The post has been vacant since mid-October; the empty podium marks the unanswered offer.

stories.name: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White the White House press secretary job
facts: On Saturday, Nov. 7, President Trump said in a Truth Social post that he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the job of White House press secretary; some outlets noted it was unclear how serious the offer was.
Speaking at a boxing event news conference in London on Saturday, White said he was flying to Washington and had a meeting on Monday; he did not say whether he would accept.
The press secretary post has been vacant since mid-October, after Karoline Leavitt left in August and her successor Katie Zacharia departed after five days.

artwork.alt: Editorial illustration split diagonally. Left: Dana White, bald in a dark suit with an open collar, speaks at a microphone-covered table at an orange-lit fight-night news conference in London, with ring ropes behind him and silhouetted reporters raising cameras and phones. Right: the White House briefing-room podium stands empty under a spotlight before a blue curtain and empty seats. A dashed jet contrail arcs from his side toward the podium. Represents Trump's Nov. 7 press secretary offer to White.
